source.note: 英文逐字稿取自 YouTube 字幕；中文為學習用翻譯。版權屬原作者，僅供個人學習。

lines.en: Hello everyone. Today we're talking about a simple idea that can change the way you move through a hard day. How to stay positive without pretending that everything is perfect.
lines.zh: 大家好。今天我們要聊一個簡單的觀念，它能改變你度過難熬日子的方式：如何保持正向，卻不必假裝一切都很完美。

lines.en: I like that last part. Sometimes people say just be positive and it can sound like don't be sad, right? Real positivity is not about hiding sadness, stress or fear. It is about seeing the problem clearly and still looking for a useful next step.
lines.zh: 我喜歡最後那部分。有時候大家說「正向一點」，聽起來卻像是「不准難過」，對吧？真正的正向不是把悲傷、壓力或恐懼藏起來，而是看清楚問題，同時仍然去找有用的下一步。

lines.en: So I can have a bad Monday and still be a positive person.
lines.zh: 所以我可以有個很糟的星期一，卻仍然是個正向的人。

lines.en: Of course. In fact, Monday is a good place to start. Many people wake up, see a long week ahead, and their first thought is, "I already feel tired."
lines.zh: 當然。事實上，星期一正好是個起點。很多人一醒來，看到漫長的一週在眼前，第一個念頭就是：「我已經覺得好累。」

lines.en: That was me this morning. My alarm rang, and my brain said, "No, thank you.
lines.zh: 今天早上的我就是這樣。鬧鐘一響，我的大腦說：「不用了，謝謝。

lines.en: Please try again tomorrow.
lines.zh: 請明天再試一次。」

lines.en: A very polite brain. But that first thought can affect the next hour, especially if we keep feeding it.
lines.zh: 好有禮貌的大腦。但那第一個念頭會影響接下來的一個小時，尤其如果我們一直去餵養它。

lines.en: What do you mean by feeding a thought?
lines.zh: 你說「餵養一個念頭」是什麼意思？

lines.en: Imagine you think today will be terrible. Then you look for proof. The traffic is slow. Your coffee is not great. And one email feels rude.
lines.zh: 想像你認為今天會很糟，然後你就開始找證據：交通很慢、咖啡不好喝，還有一封 email 讓你覺得很沒禮貌。

lines.en: And suddenly I say, "See, I knew this day was bad."
lines.zh: 然後我突然就說：「你看，我就知道今天很糟。」

lines.en: Yes. Your mind starts to notice only the things that match the first negative thought. But you can train yourself to notice more than one side of the day.
lines.zh: 對。你的心會開始只注意那些符合第一個負面念頭的事。但你可以訓練自己，看見一天當中不只一面。

lines.en: So the goal is not everything is wonderful. It is more like this part is hard but the whole day is not ruined.
lines.zh: 所以目標不是「一切都很美好」，比較像是「這部分很難，但整天並沒有毀掉」。

lines.en: Exactly. That is a much healthier kind of positive thinking. It is balanced not fake.
lines.zh: 沒錯。那是健康得多的正向思考——是平衡的，不是假裝的。

lines.en: I need that. When one small thing goes wrong, I sometimes act like the whole week is broken.
lines.zh: 我需要這個。一件小事出錯時，我有時候會表現得好像整個禮拜都毀了。

lines.en: Then here is our first simple habit.
lines.zh: 那這就是我們第一個簡單的習慣。

lines.en: Listen to your self-talk. Self-talk is the quiet language you use inside your own mind.
lines.zh: 留意你的自我對話。自我對話就是你在自己心裡說話的那種安靜語言。

lines.en: Like the little voice that says you can do this or you always mess things up.
lines.zh: 就像那個會說「你做得到」或「你老是把事情搞砸」的小聲音。

lines.en: Yes, we all have that voice. The important question is not whether it is always positive, but whether it is fair and useful.
lines.zh: 對，我們都有那個聲音。重要的問題不是它是否總是正向，而是它是否公平、是否有用。

lines.en: Fair and useful. I like that because I'm amazing at everything is positive, but it is not very believable, right? A better sentence might be, I don't know how to do this yet, but I can learn one part today.
lines.zh: 公平又有用，我喜歡。因為「我什麼都超厲害」雖然很正向，但不太可信，對吧？更好的句子可能是：「我還不會做這個，但我今天可以先學會一部分。」

lines.en: That feels calmer. It gives me something to do.
lines.zh: 那感覺比較平靜，也給了我一件可以做的事。

lines.en: And that matters. When a thought gives you a clear action, it can help you move instead of making you feel stuck.
lines.zh: 而這很重要。當一個念頭給你明確的行動，它能幫你往前走，而不是讓你覺得卡住。

lines.en: Can we try a few negative thoughts and change them?
lines.zh: 我們可以試幾個負面念頭，把它們改寫嗎？

lines.en: Sure. Here is one. I made a mistake, so I'm bad at my job.
lines.zh: 當然。這是一個：「我犯了錯，所以我不擅長我的工作。」

lines.en: Maybe I can say I made a mistake. I need to fix it and learn from it.
lines.zh: 也許我可以說：「我犯了錯，我需要修正它，並從中學習。」

lines.en: Perfect. You did not lie to yourself.
lines.zh: 很好。你沒有對自己說謊。

lines.en: You admitted the mistake, but you did not turn one mistake into a story about who you are. Okay, another one. My English is terrible because I didn't understand that video.
lines.zh: 你承認了錯誤，但沒有把一個錯誤變成一個「你是什麼樣的人」的故事。好，再一個：「我的英文很爛，因為我看不懂那支影片。」

lines.en: Try this. That video was difficult for me today. I can listen again, slow it down, or choose something easier first.
lines.zh: 試試這樣說：「那支影片今天對我來說很難。我可以再聽一次、放慢速度，或先選簡單一點的。」

lines.en: That sounds much better than I'm just bad at English.
lines.zh: 那聽起來比「我就是英文很爛」好多了。

lines.en: And notice the difference. One sentence closes the door. The other sentence keeps the door open.
lines.zh: 注意其中的差別：一個句子把門關上，另一個句子讓門保持開著。

lines.en: I think many learners need to hear that.
lines.zh: 我想很多學習者需要聽到這個。

lines.en: We often judge our whole ability from one hard moment.
lines.zh: 我們常常因為一個困難的時刻，就否定自己全部的能力。

lines.en: Yes, especially when we are tired. A tired mind can be very dramatic.
lines.zh: 對，尤其是我們累的時候。疲累的心可以非常戲劇化。

lines.en: Mind deserves an award sometimes. Then maybe give it a smaller role. When a negative thought comes, you can say that is one thought. It is not the full story.
lines.zh: 這樣的心有時候真該頒個獎。那也許可以給它小一點的角色。負面念頭出現時，你可以說：「那只是一個念頭，它不是故事的全部。」

lines.en: Wait, that sentence is useful. It is not the full story.
lines.zh: 等等，這句很好用。「它不是故事的全部。」

lines.en: Very useful. You can use it when you are worried, embarrassed, angry or disappointed.
lines.zh: 非常好用。當你擔心、尷尬、生氣或失望時都可以用。

lines.en: For example, I had a bad meeting, but that is not the full story of my work.
lines.zh: 例如：「我開了一場很糟的會，但那不是我工作的全部。」

lines.en: Good. or I feel lonely tonight, but that is not the full story of my life.
lines.zh: 很好。或是：「我今晚覺得很孤單，但那不是我人生的全部。」

lines.en: That feels positive without becoming silly.
lines.zh: 這樣感覺很正向，又不會流於傻氣。

lines.en: Exactly. Positive thinking should help you face reality, not run away from it.
lines.zh: 沒錯。正向思考應該幫你面對現實，而不是逃避現實。

lines.en: So, what should I do when my mind is very negative and I cannot change the thought easily?
lines.zh: 那當我的心很負面，又沒辦法輕易轉念時，我該怎麼辦？

lines.en: Change the next few minutes instead. Do something small that supports your body and mind. Like what?
lines.zh: 那就改變接下來的幾分鐘。做一件支持你身心的小事。比如說？

lines.en: Stand up, drink some water, or open the curtains, take a short walk, put your phone away for 10 minutes, or send a message to someone you trust.
lines.zh: 站起來、喝點水，或拉開窗簾、散個短步、把手機收起來十分鐘，或傳訊息給一個你信任的人。

lines.en: That sounds almost too simple.
lines.zh: 那聽起來簡單到有點不可思議。

lines.en: Simple does not mean useless. Small actions can change your energy, and better energy can make better thinking easier. I have noticed that if I stay in bed scrolling, my problems feel huge. If I get up, shower, and eat something,
lines.zh: 簡單不代表沒用。小小的行動能改變你的能量，而更好的能量能讓好的思考更容易發生。我發現如果我賴在床上一直滑手機，問題就顯得很巨大；如果我起床、洗澡、吃點東西，

lines.en: they often feel smaller and easier to face.
lines.zh: 問題往往就會變小，也比較容易面對。

lines.en: That is a good example. You do not need to wait until you feel positive before you act.
lines.zh: 這是個好例子。你不需要等到覺得正向了才行動。

lines.en: So, action can come first. Yes, sometimes you act with care first and your feelings slowly follow.
lines.zh: 所以行動可以先來。對，有時候你先用心去做，感覺會慢慢跟上。

lines.en: That changes the idea for me. I thought staying positive was mostly about thoughts.
lines.zh: 這改變了我的想法。我以為保持正向主要跟想法有關。

lines.en: Thoughts matter, but your daily habits matter, too. Sleep, food, movement, rest, and connection can all support the way you handle stress. And if I sleep 4 hours, drink five coffees and argue online all morning, positive thinking may have a hard job.
lines.zh: 想法很重要，但你的日常習慣也很重要。睡眠、飲食、運動、休息和人際連結，都能支持你處理壓力的方式。如果我只睡四小時、喝五杯咖啡、整個早上在網路上跟人吵架，正向思考恐怕會很辛苦。

lines.en: A very hard job. Your mind lives in your body. So care for both.
lines.zh: 非常辛苦。你的心住在你的身體裡，所以兩者都要照顧。

lines.en: Okay, we have self-talk and small actions. But what about worry? That is where I get stuck.
lines.zh: 好，我們已經有自我對話和小行動了。那擔心呢？我總是卡在那裡。

lines.en: Then let's talk about control. A lot of stress comes from trying to solve things that are not ours to control, like what other people think about me.
lines.zh: 那我們來談談「掌控」。很多壓力來自試圖解決那些不是我們能掌控的事，像是別人怎麼看我。

lines.en: Yes. Also, the weather, the past, every piece of news, another person's mood, or whether everyone agrees with you.
lines.zh: 對。還有天氣、過去、每一則新聞、別人的心情，或是不是每個人都同意你。

lines.en: I know I cannot control those things, but my brain still wants to work on them.
lines.zh: 我知道那些事我控制不了，但我的大腦還是想去處理它們。

lines.en: Mine, too. So, I use a simple question.
lines.zh: 我也是。所以我會用一個簡單的問題。

lines.en: Is there something useful I can do about this today?
lines.zh: 「今天，我能為這件事做點什麼有用的嗎？」

lines.en: And if the answer is no, then I try to let the thought pass and move my attention to something I can do.
lines.zh: 如果答案是否定的，我就試著讓這個念頭過去，把注意力轉到我能做的事情上。

lines.en: Give me an example.
lines.zh: 舉個例子吧。

lines.en: Maybe you are worried about a job interview tomorrow.
lines.zh: 也許你在擔心明天的工作面試。

lines.en: You cannot control the interviewer's mood or the final decision. But I can prepare my answers, choose my clothes, sleep on time, and arrive early.
lines.zh: 你控制不了面試官的心情或最後的決定，但我可以準備好回答、挑好衣服、準時睡覺，然後提早到場。

lines.en: Exactly.
lines.zh: 沒錯。

lines.en: That is what focus on means here. You choose where to place your attention.
lines.zh: 這就是這裡所說的「專注於」（focus on）：你選擇把注意力放在哪裡。

lines.en: So I focus on preparation, not on trying to control the future.
lines.zh: 所以我專注在準備上，而不是試圖控制未來。

lines.en: Yes, that does not remove all fear, but it gives your fear less space.
lines.zh: 對，這不會消除所有恐懼，但會讓恐懼的空間變小。

lines.en: I like to write things down when I worry. Is that useful, too?
lines.zh: 我擔心的時候喜歡把事情寫下來。這樣也有用嗎？

lines.en: It can be. You can make two short lists.
lines.zh: 可以有用。你可以列兩張短短的清單。

lines.en: I can do something and I cannot control this.
lines.zh: 「我可以做的事」和「我無法控制的事」。

lines.en: That sounds easier than thinking about everything at once.
lines.zh: 這聽起來比一次想所有事情容易。

lines.en: That is the point. When worries stay only in your head, they can feel like one big cloud. On paper, you can often see the next step more clearly.
lines.zh: 這就是重點。擔憂只放在腦袋裡時，會像一大片烏雲；寫在紙上，你往往更能看清下一步。

lines.en: Let me try. I'm worried because my friend has not answered my message.
lines.zh: 我試試看。我很擔心，因為我朋友還沒回我訊息。

lines.en: Good. What can you control?
lines.zh: 很好。你能控制什麼？

lines.en: I can send one kind followup later or I can wait. I cannot control when my friend answers. Exactly. Now you have a calm plan and I do not need to check my phone every 30 seconds.
lines.zh: 我可以晚點再傳一則友善的追蹤訊息，或者我可以等。我控制不了朋友什麼時候回。沒錯。現在你有個冷靜的計畫，我也不用每 30 秒就檢查一次手機。

lines.en: Correct. Your thumb will survive.
lines.zh: 正確。你的大拇指會活下來的。

lines.en: I'm not sure my thumb believes you.
lines.zh: 我不確定我的大拇指相信你。

lines.en: Then give it a small vacation.
lines.zh: 那就讓它放個小假吧。

lines.en: Done. But what if I have a real problem like money stress or a difficult family situation? Saying stay positive can feel too small.
lines.zh: 好。但如果我遇到的是真正的問題，像是金錢壓力或困難的家庭狀況呢？說「保持正向」好像太微不足道了。

lines.en: That is important. Positive thinking does not take the place of real help, real planning or difficult conversations.
lines.zh: 這點很重要。正向思考不能取代真正的幫助、真正的規劃，或困難的對話。

lines.en: So if the problem needs action, positivity should help me take action, not avoid it.
lines.zh: 所以如果問題需要行動，正向應該幫我採取行動，而不是逃避它。

lines.en: Exactly. You may need to make a budget, ask for support, talk to a manager, see a doctor, or speak with someone you trust.
lines.zh: 沒錯。你可能需要做預算、尋求支援、跟主管談、去看醫生，或跟你信任的人聊聊。

lines.en: That feels more honest. Positivity is not magic. It is a way to keep moving while you deal with real life.
lines.zh: 這感覺比較誠實。正向不是魔法，而是一種在面對真實生活時持續前進的方式。

lines.en: Well said. And that brings us to goals because goals can give your mind direction.
lines.zh: 說得好。這就帶到了目標，因為目標能給你的心一個方向。

lines.en: Goals also make me nervous. I write 12 goals in January and forget 11 of them by February.
lines.zh: 目標也讓我緊張。我一月寫了 12 個目標，到了二月就忘了 11 個。

lines.en: Then the problem may not be you. The goals may be too big, too many, or too unclear. I usually write things like get healthy, improve English, save money, become a new person.
lines.zh: 那問題可能不在你。可能是目標太大、太多或太模糊。我通常會寫「變健康、英文進步、存錢、成為全新的人」這類的。

lines.en: That is enough work for four different lives.
lines.zh: 那足夠四個不同的人生去做了。

lines.en: So, what should I write instead?
lines.zh: 那我應該改寫什麼？

lines.en: Choose one small step you can repeat.
lines.zh: 選一個你能重複做的小步驟。

lines.en: For health, maybe walk for 15 minutes after dinner. For English, listen to 10 minutes of easy English each morning.
lines.zh: 健康方面，也許晚餐後走路 15 分鐘；英文方面，每天早上聽 10 分鐘簡單的英文。

lines.en: For money, maybe check what I spend for one week before I make a big plan.
lines.zh: 金錢方面，也許在做大計畫之前，先記錄自己一週花了多少錢。

lines.en: Good. Small goals reduce the feeling of I have to fix my whole life now.
lines.zh: 很好。小目標能減少「我現在就得修正整個人生」的那種感覺。

lines.en: That sentence is exactly what my brain says at 1:00 a.m.
lines.zh: 那句話完全就是我的大腦在凌晨一點會說的。

lines.en: At 1:00 a.m., your brain should not be the manager of your future.
lines.zh: 凌晨一點的時候，你的大腦不應該當你未來的主管。

lines.en: Please tell my brain that I just did. A small step gives you a clear next move. And when you repeat it, you build trust in yourself.
lines.zh: 請幫我轉告我的大腦……我剛剛說了。小步驟給你一個明確的下一步，而當你重複去做，你就在建立對自己的信任。

lines.en: What do you mean by trust in yourself?
lines.zh: 你說「對自己的信任」是什麼意思？

lines.en: You start to believe when I say I will do something small, I usually do it.
lines.zh: 你開始相信：當我說要做一件小事時，我通常都會做到。

lines.en: That feeling is powerful.
lines.zh: 那種感覺很有力量。

lines.en: So confidence does not always come before action.
lines.zh: 所以自信不一定在行動之前出現。

lines.en: Right? Very often confidence grows after you act. That is useful for English too.
lines.zh: 對吧？很多時候，自信是在你行動之後才長出來的。這對學英文也很有用。

lines.en: I may not feel confident speaking, but I can still say three sentences today.
lines.zh: 我可能對開口說英文沒自信，但我今天還是可以說三個句子。

lines.en: Exactly. And tomorrow maybe three more.
lines.zh: 沒錯。明天也許再多說三句。

lines.en: Positivity grows when you see evidence that you can move.
lines.zh: 當你看到自己能前進的證據，正向就會增長。

lines.en: What if I miss a day? I often become very negative after that.
lines.zh: 如果我漏了一天呢？之後我常會變得很負面。

lines.en: Then do not turn one missed day into a story about your character. Say, "I missed today. I can return tomorrow."
lines.zh: 那就別把漏掉的一天變成一個關於你品格的故事。就說：「我今天漏了，明天可以回來繼續。」

lines.en: No punishment, no dramatic speech.
lines.zh: 不用懲罰，也不用來一段戲劇化的演講。

lines.en: No dramatic speech needed. Returning is more useful than judging yourself.
lines.zh: 不需要戲劇化的演講。回到正軌比評判自己更有用。

lines.en: That is a good rule. Return quickly.
lines.zh: 這是個好規則：快點回來。

lines.en: Yes, staying positive often means returning. Return to your plan, your routine, your people, or your healthy habits. And that connects to another question. What happens when life knocks you down for more than one day?
lines.zh: 對，保持正向常常就是「回來」：回到你的計畫、你的日常、你的人，或你的健康習慣。這也連到另一個問題：如果生活把你擊倒不只一天呢？

lines.en: Then you may need time. A breakup, a loss, a failure, or a big disappointment cannot always be solved with one walk and a glass of water.
lines.zh: 那你可能需要時間。分手、失去、失敗或很大的失望，不一定能靠一次散步和一杯水解決。

lines.en: I'm glad you said that. Sometimes motivational advice makes pain sound too easy.
lines.zh: 很高興你這麼說。有時候勵志建議把痛苦說得太簡單了。

lines.en: Pain is not easy. If something hurts, you are allowed to feel it. You can be positive and still cry.
lines.zh: 痛苦並不簡單。如果某件事讓你受傷，你有權利去感受它。你可以既正向又哭泣。

lines.en: So staying positive during a hard season may look very quiet.
lines.zh: 所以在艱難時期保持正向，看起來可能非常安靜。

lines.en: Yes, it may look like getting out of bed, eating breakfast, going to work, or calling one safe person.
lines.zh: 對，它看起來可能只是起床、吃早餐、去上班，或打電話給一個讓你安心的人。

lines.en: Not a big smile, just one normal action.
lines.zh: 不是燦爛的笑容，只是一個平常的行動。

lines.en: Exactly. And over time you can begin to bounce back.
lines.zh: 沒錯。隨著時間過去，你就能開始重新振作（bounce back）。

lines.en: Bounce back means recover after something difficult. Right.
lines.zh: bounce back 的意思是在困難之後恢復過來。對吧。

lines.en: Yes. You fall, life hurts and then little by little you find your strength again.
lines.zh: 對。你跌倒了、生活讓你受傷，然後一點一點地重新找回力量。

lines.en: I remember losing an important opportunity once. For 2 days I kept thinking this was my only chance.
lines.zh: 我記得有一次錯過了一個很重要的機會。整整兩天，我一直覺得那是我唯一的機會。

lines.en: That sounds painful. What helped? A friend asked me a simple question. What can you still do this week? That changed something.
lines.zh: 聽起來很痛苦。後來是什麼幫了你？一個朋友問了我一個簡單的問題：「這禮拜你還能做什麼？」那改變了一些事。

lines.en: Because it moved you from the closed door to the next possible door.
lines.zh: 因為它把你從那扇關上的門，帶到下一扇可能的門前。

lines.en: Exactly. I updated my work, sent two new emails, and talked to someone in the same field. I still felt disappointed, but I was moving again. That is a good example of working through a problem. To work through something means you deal
lines.zh: 沒錯。我更新了作品、寄出兩封新的 email，還跟同領域的人聊了聊。我還是很失望，但我又開始前進了。這就是 work through a problem（一步步處理問題）的好例子。work through something 的意思是你

lines.en: with it step by step instead of expecting it to disappear at once.
lines.zh: 一步一步去處理它，而不是期待它一下子就消失。

lines.en: So I can work through fear, work through a problem or work through a difficult feeling.
lines.zh: 所以我可以 work through 恐懼、work through 一個問題，或 work through 一種難受的感覺。

lines.en: Yes. And you do not have to work through everything alone. Support from other people matters.
lines.zh: 對。而且你不必獨自面對所有事。來自別人的支持很重要。

lines.en: That part is easy to forget when we want to look strong.
lines.zh: 當我們想要看起來很堅強時，很容易忘記這一點。

lines.en: It is. But asking for help is not the opposite of being positive. Sometimes it is the most useful positive action you can take.
lines.zh: 確實。但尋求幫助並不是正向的相反。有時候，那正是你能採取的最有用的正向行動。

lines.en: Maybe saying, "I'm having a hard week.
lines.zh: 也許可以說：「我這禮拜過得很辛苦。

lines.en: Can we talk?"
lines.zh: 我們可以聊聊嗎？」

lines.en: Perfect, clear, simple, and honest.
lines.zh: 完美——清楚、簡單又誠實。

lines.en: What if I do not want advice? Sometimes I just want someone to listen.
lines.zh: 如果我不想聽建議呢？有時候我只是想要有人聽我說。

lines.en: Then say that, too. I don't need you to fix it. I just need someone to listen for a few minutes.
lines.zh: 那也可以直說：「我不需要你幫我解決，我只是需要有人聽我說幾分鐘。」

lines.en: That is a great sentence for real life.
lines.zh: 這是真實生活中很好用的一句話。

lines.en: And it shows something important.
lines.zh: 而且它顯示了一件很重要的事。

lines.en: Positive people do not always have answers. They know how to stay connected while they look for answers.
lines.zh: 正向的人不一定總是有答案。他們懂得在尋找答案的同時，和別人保持連結。

lines.en: So far, staying positive sounds much more practical than I expected.
lines.zh: 到目前為止，保持正向聽起來比我想像的實際多了。

lines.en: Good. Now, let's make it even more practical with a short challenge for the listener.
lines.zh: 很好。現在我們用一個給聽眾的小挑戰，讓它更實際一點。

lines.en: All right, everyone. No notebook needed unless you want one. Think of one small problem from this week. Nothing too private or too heavy. Just one normal problem.
lines.zh: 好，各位，不需要筆記本，除非你想用。想一個這禮拜遇到的小問題，不要太私密或太沉重，就一個普通的問題。

lines.en: Maybe you are behind on work, worried about your English, tired after a busy week, or nervous about a conversation.
lines.zh: 也許你工作進度落後、擔心自己的英文、忙了一週很累，或是對一場談話感到緊張。

lines.en: Now finish this sentence in your mind.
lines.zh: 現在，在心裡完成這個句子。

lines.en: The part I can control is I'll do one. I'm behind on work. The part I can control is doing the most important task for 20 minutes.
lines.zh: 「我能掌控的部分是……」我先來一個。我工作進度落後。我能掌控的部分，是花 20 分鐘做最重要的那件工作。

lines.en: Good. Now a second sentence. My next small step is My next small step is closing my messages and starting that task.
lines.zh: 很好。現在第二句：「我的下一個小步驟是……」我的下一個小步驟，是關掉訊息，開始做那件工作。

lines.en: Excellent. Last sentence. I do not need to solve everything today.
lines.zh: 太棒了。最後一句：「我今天不需要解決所有事。」

lines.en: That one makes my shoulders relax. Those three sentences are simple but they move your attention from panic to action.
lines.zh: 這句讓我的肩膀放鬆了。這三個句子很簡單，但能把你的注意力從慌張轉到行動上。

lines.en: Can we do one for English learners too?
lines.zh: 我們也可以幫英文學習者做一組嗎？

lines.en: Sure. Imagine the thought is I cannot understand native speakers.
lines.zh: 當然。想像那個念頭是：「我聽不懂母語人士說話。」

lines.en: The part I can control is choosing easier audio and listening every day.
lines.zh: 我能掌控的部分，是選擇簡單一點的音檔，並且每天聽。

lines.en: My next small step is listening to five minutes and writing down two phrases I hear. And I do not need to understand every native speaker today.
lines.zh: 我的下一個小步驟，是聽五分鐘，寫下我聽到的兩個片語。而且我今天不需要聽懂每一個母語人士。

lines.en: Perfect. That is realistic positivity.
lines.zh: 完美。這就是務實的正向。

lines.en: I also think comparison makes positivity difficult. I can feel good. Then I open social media and suddenly my life looks small.
lines.zh: 我也覺得「比較」讓正向變得很難。我本來心情很好，然後打開社群媒體，突然覺得自己的人生好渺小。

lines.en: Comparison can change your mood very quickly. You often see another person's best moment and compare it with your normal day. My vacation photo versus my laundry.
lines.zh: 比較可以很快改變你的心情。你常常是拿別人最美好的一刻，來跟自己平凡的一天比。像是他的度假照 vs. 我的待洗衣物。

lines.en: Exactly. And your laundry usually loses.
lines.zh: 沒錯。而且你的待洗衣物通常會輸。

lines.en: Poor laundry. It never had a chance.
lines.zh: 可憐的衣服，它從來就沒有勝算。

lines.en: When comparison starts, return to your own life. Ask what matters to me today.
lines.zh: 當你開始比較時，回到自己的生活。問問自己：「今天對我來說重要的是什麼？」

lines.en: Not how do I become that person by Friday?
lines.zh: 而不是「我要怎麼在禮拜五之前變成那個人？」

lines.en: Right? Your life does not need to look like someone else's life to have value.
lines.zh: 對吧？你的人生不需要看起來像別人的人生，才有價值。

lines.en: Would gratitude help here?
lines.zh: 感恩在這裡會有幫助嗎？

lines.en: It can if you keep it simple. Gratitude means noticing something good that is already here.
lines.zh: 如果保持簡單，就會有幫助。感恩的意思是注意到已經存在的美好事物。

lines.en: Like a good meal, a friend's message, a quiet room, or understanding one more sentence in English.
lines.zh: 像是一頓好吃的飯、朋友傳來的訊息、一個安靜的房間，或多聽懂了一句英文。

lines.en: Exactly. You do not need a perfect day to find one good thing in it.
lines.zh: 沒錯。你不需要完美的一天，也能在其中找到一件好事。

lines.en: I like doing that at night. I ask, "What went okay today?" That is a strong question because it is realistic. You are not asking was today amazing. You were looking for one part that went okay.
lines.zh: 我喜歡晚上做這件事。我會問：「今天有什麼事還不錯？」這是個很有力的問題，因為它很實際。你不是在問今天是不是超棒，而是在找其中一個還不錯的部分。

lines.en: Yesterday my answer was I made a really good sandwich.
lines.zh: 昨天我的答案是：我做了一個超好吃的三明治。

lines.en: That counts.
lines.zh: 那也算數。

lines.en: Thank you. I was proud of that sandwich.
lines.zh: 謝謝。我對那個三明治很自豪。

lines.en: Small good moments count because your life is mostly made of ordinary moments, not huge events. That may be my favorite idea today.
lines.zh: 小小的美好時刻都算數，因為你的人生大部分是由平凡時刻組成，而不是由重大事件組成。這可能是我今天最喜歡的觀念。

lines.en: Then remember it when you think happiness must arrive as a big change.
lines.zh: 那當你覺得幸福一定要以巨大改變的形式出現時，就記得這一點。

lines.en: Often it grows from small choices you repeat.
lines.zh: 幸福往往是從你重複做出的小選擇中長出來的。

lines.en: I want to ask about positive people too.
lines.zh: 我也想問問關於「正向的人」。

lines.en: Can the people around us affect how positive we feel?
lines.zh: 我們身邊的人會影響我們有多正向嗎？

lines.en: Yes, we are affected by the way people speak, complain, encourage and respond to problems. So, should I avoid every negative person?
lines.zh: 會，別人說話、抱怨、鼓勵和面對問題的方式都會影響我們。那我應該避開每一個負面的人嗎？

lines.en: No. Everyone has negative days, but you can notice which relationships leave you feeling supported and which ones leave you tired all the time.
lines.zh: 不用。每個人都有負面的日子，但你可以留意哪些關係讓你覺得被支持，哪些總是讓你覺得很累。

lines.en: And I guess I should also ask what kind of energy I bring to other people.
lines.zh: 我想我也應該問問自己，我帶給別人的是什麼樣的能量。

lines.en: That is a mature question. Staying positive is not only about finding support. It is also about giving support in a healthy way.
lines.zh: 這是個成熟的問題。保持正向不只是找到支持，也包括用健康的方式給予支持。

lines.en: For example, instead of saying, "Your problem is nothing," I could say, "That sounds hard. What do you need right now?"
lines.zh: 例如，與其說「你的問題沒什麼啦」，我可以說「聽起來好辛苦。你現在需要什麼？」

lines.en: Much better. That is positive and respectful.
lines.zh: 好多了。那樣既正向又尊重對方。

lines.en: Because telling someone to stop feeling bad can make them feel worse.
lines.zh: 因為叫別人不要難過，反而可能讓他們更難受。

lines.en: Exactly. We do not need to force good feelings. We can make room for the real feeling and then look for the next helpful step. So, if my friend says, "I failed an exam." I should not say, "Be positive. It doesn't matter,
lines.zh: 沒錯。我們不需要強迫自己產生好的感覺。我們可以先給真實的感受一些空間，再去找下一個有幫助的步驟。所以如果我朋友說「我考試沒過」，我不應該說「正向一點，這不重要，

lines.en: right?" You could say, "I'm sorry. I know you worked hard." When you're ready, we can think about what to do next.
lines.zh: 對吧？」你可以說：「我很遺憾，我知道你很努力。等你準備好了，我們再一起想想接下來怎麼做。」

lines.en: That sounds much kinder.
lines.zh: 那聽起來溫柔多了。

lines.en: Kindness is a big part of positivity, especially the way you speak to yourself.
lines.zh: 善意是正向很重要的一部分，尤其是你對自己說話的方式。

lines.en: I am much kinder to my friends than I am to myself. Many people are. So here is a useful check. If your friend made the same mistake, would you speak to them the way you speak to yourself?
lines.zh: 我對朋友比對自己溫柔多了。很多人都是這樣。所以這裡有個好用的檢查方法：如果你的朋友犯了同樣的錯，你會用對自己說話的方式跟他說話嗎？

lines.en: Usually no. I would never tell a friend.
lines.zh: 通常不會。我絕對不會跟朋友說：

lines.en: You are terrible and you will never improve.
lines.zh: 「你很糟糕，你永遠不會進步。」

lines.en: Then do not make that your daily self-talk.
lines.zh: 那就別讓那句話成為你每天的自我對話。

lines.en: Maybe I can say this was not my best day, but I can try again. Excellent.
lines.zh: 也許我可以說：「今天不是我最好的一天，但我可以再試一次。」太棒了。

lines.en: Calm, honest, and forward-looking.
lines.zh: 冷靜、誠實，而且向前看。

lines.en: We have covered a lot. Can we make a simple daily routine from all of this?
lines.zh: 我們聊了好多。可以把這些整理成一個簡單的每日習慣嗎？

lines.en: Yes. Try three short moments. Morning, middle of the day, and evening.
lines.zh: 可以。試試三個短短的時刻：早上、中午和晚上。

lines.en: What happens in the morning?
lines.zh: 早上要做什麼？

lines.en: Before you check everything on your phone, choose one helpful thought.
lines.zh: 在你把手機上的東西全部看一遍之前，先選一個有幫助的念頭。

lines.en: Something like, I only need to take the next step. middle of the day.
lines.zh: 像是：「我只需要走出下一步。」然後是中午。

lines.en: Check your self-talk. If your mind is becoming very negative, ask is this the full story and what can I control now?
lines.zh: 檢查你的自我對話。如果你的心變得很負面，就問：「這是故事的全部嗎？我現在能掌控什麼？」

lines.en: And in the evening, find one thing that went okay.
lines.zh: 到了晚上，找一件今天還不錯的事。

lines.en: Yes. Then choose one small step for tomorrow. That is enough.
lines.zh: 對。然後為明天選一個小步驟。這樣就夠了。

lines.en: I like that it takes only a few minutes.
lines.zh: 我喜歡它只需要幾分鐘。

lines.en: It does not become another big job.
lines.zh: 它不會變成另一件大工程。

lines.en: That is important. A helpful habit should support your life, not become one more reason to feel guilty.
lines.zh: 這很重要。一個好習慣應該支持你的生活，而不是變成又一個讓你內疚的理由。

lines.en: And if I forget the routine for three days, return on day four.
lines.zh: 如果我忘了這個習慣三天，就在第四天回來。

lines.en: You really like that word return because it is more useful than perfection.
lines.zh: 你真的很喜歡「回來」這個詞。因為它比完美更有用。

lines.en: Fair point.
lines.zh: 說得有道理。

lines.en: Before we finish, let's review five useful words and expressions you heard today.
lines.zh: 結束之前，我們來複習今天聽到的五個實用單字和說法。

lines.en: I'm ready. Let's keep the meaning simple. Expression one self-talk.
lines.zh: 我準備好了。意思講簡單一點就好。說法一：self-talk。

lines.en: Self-talk is the language you use inside your own mind. Example, I'm trying to make my self-talk kinder when I make a mistake.
lines.zh: self-talk 是你在自己心裡使用的語言。例句：I'm trying to make my self-talk kinder when I make a mistake.（我犯錯時，試著讓自我對話更溫柔一點。）

lines.en: Expression two, focus on. It means to give your attention to one thing.
lines.zh: 說法二：focus on，意思是把注意力放在一件事上。

lines.en: Example, I can't control the result. So, I'll focus on my preparation.
lines.zh: 例句：I can't control the result. So, I'll focus on my preparation.（我控制不了結果，所以我會專注在準備上。）

lines.en: Expression three, small step. A small step is one easy action that moves you forward. Example, my small step today is studying English for 10 minutes.
lines.zh: 說法三：small step。small step 是一個能讓你往前走的簡單行動。例句：my small step today is studying English for 10 minutes.（我今天的小步驟是讀英文 10 分鐘。）

lines.en: Expression four, bounce back. It means to recover after a difficult time.
lines.zh: 說法四：bounce back，意思是在困難時期之後恢復過來。

lines.en: Example, she was disappointed but she slowly bounced back. Expression five, work through. It means to deal with a problem or feeling step by step.
lines.zh: 例句：she was disappointed but she slowly bounced back.（她很失望，但慢慢重新振作了。）說法五：work through，意思是一步步處理一個問題或一種感受。

lines.en: Example, I'm talking with a friend to work through this problem.
lines.zh: 例句：I'm talking with a friend to work through this problem.（我正在和朋友聊，一步步解決這個問題。）

lines.en: Nice. Those five expressions fit the whole idea of today.
lines.zh: 很好。這五個說法正好貫穿今天的主題。

lines.en: They do. And here is the main message.
lines.zh: 沒錯。這是今天的核心訊息：

lines.en: Staying positive does not mean saying everything is fine when it is not. It means I can say this is hard but I still have a next step.
lines.zh: 保持正向不是在事情不好時還說一切都很好，而是能說「這很難，但我仍然有下一步」。

lines.en: Yes. Notice your self-talk. Focus on what you can control. Choose a small step. Stay connected and give yourself time to bounce back.
lines.zh: 對。留意你的自我對話、專注於你能掌控的事、選一個小步驟、與人保持連結，並給自己時間重新振作。

lines.en: And if today is a difficult day, maybe your positive action is very small. Eat something. Go outside for 5 minutes.
lines.zh: 如果今天是很難熬的一天，也許你的正向行動會非常小：吃點東西、到外面走五分鐘。

lines.en: Answer one message or simply rest without judging yourself.
lines.zh: 回一則訊息，或只是好好休息，不去評判自己。

lines.en: That still counts. Progress can be quiet. Before we go, choose one sentence from today and keep it with you. Mine is I do not need to solve everything today.
lines.zh: 那仍然算數。進步可以是安靜的。結束之前，從今天挑一句話帶在身上。我的是「我今天不需要解決所有事」。

lines.en: Mine is this is not the full story. A hard moment is real, but it is only one part of a much bigger life.
lines.zh: 我的是「這不是故事的全部」。困難的時刻是真實的，但它只是更大人生中的一部分。

lines.en: Thanks for spending this time with us.
lines.zh: 謝謝你花時間和我們在一起。

lines.en: Take care of your mind. Be kind to yourself. Keep practicing your English.
lines.zh: 照顧好你的心，善待自己，持續練習英文。

lines.en: And I'll see you next time. Bye.
lines.zh: 我們下次見，掰掰。
